title: Classification of Mountains
subject: Geography
description: This diagram classifies mountains into Fold (Young and Old), Block, Volcanic, and Residual types, explaining their formation mechanisms and providing examples.
mermaidCode:
graph TD
A[Classification of Mountains] --> B[Fold Mountains]
B --> B1(Formed by folding of crustal rocks)
B --> B2(Compressional forces)
B --> B3[Young Fold Mountains]
B3 --> B3a(High, rugged, geologically young)
B3a --> B3b(Himalayas, Andes, Rockies, Alps)
B --> B4[Old Fold Mountains]
B4 --> B4a(Older, heavily eroded, lower height)
B4a --> B4b(Appalachians, Urals, Aravallis)
A --> C[Block Mountains]
C --> C1(Crustal blocks displaced vertically along faults)
C --> C2(Uplifted blocks: Horsts)
C --> C3(Lowered blocks: Grabens/Rift Valleys)
C3 --> C4(Vosges, Black Forest, Sierra Nevada)
A --> D[Volcanic (Accumulation) Mountains]
D --> D1(Built by successive eruptions of lava, ash, debris)
D1 --> D2(Mount Fuji, Mount Kilimanjaro, Mount St. Helens)
A --> E[Residual (Dissected) Mountains]
E --> E1(Remnants of eroded plateaus or high plains)
E1 --> E2(Vindhyas, Satpuras, Eastern Ghats)
